questions.q: Why can fast-tracking reduce schedule duration?
o: Later construction packages can start while later design packages are still being completed
questions.n: Overlapping phases shortens elapsed time but usually increases coordination demands.

questions.q: Which operative word traditionally indicates a mandatory requirement placed on the Contractor?
questions.n: 'Shall' is traditionally used for mandatory contractor obligations in prescriptive specification language.

questions.q: Why are defined operative words important in specifications?
o: They clarify responsibility, obligation, permission, and intent
questions.n: Consistent verbs reduce ambiguity over who must do what and whether a requirement is mandatory or optional.

questions.q: When the Contractor must choose from a limited pair of alternatives, which traditional construction is appropriate?
questions.n: The traditional wording 'shall either … or' indicates a mandatory selection between limited listed alternatives.

questions.q: How does dimetric differ from isometric projection?
o: Dimetric uses two equal axis scales, while isometric uses equal scale on all three principal axes
questions.n: The distinction lies in the relative foreshortening of principal axes.

questions.q: What is a proprietary specification?
o: A specification that identifies a particular product, manufacturer, system, or process
A specification containing no product information
questions.n: Proprietary specifications identify products or systems by specific manufacturer or trade designation.

questions.q: What is topping out?
o: Placing the final major structural member at the top of a building frame
Applying the final coat of paint
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction
questions.n: Topping out marks completion of the principal structural frame.

questions.q: Which axonometric projection has two principal axes equally foreshortened and the third at a different scale?
questions.n: Dimetric projection uses two equal axis scales and a third different scale.

questions.q: What relationship allows two or more activities to proceed independently at the same time?
questions.n: Parallel activities occur concurrently rather than waiting for one another to finish.

questions.q: What is life-cycle cost?
o: The total cost of owning, operating, maintaining, and disposing of a facility over its useful life
questions.n: Life-cycle cost considers costs beyond initial construction.

questions.q: What is fast-track delivery?
o: Overlapping design and construction phases to shorten total project duration
questions.n: Fast-tracking intentionally overlaps design packages and construction activities.

questions.q: Which type of network logic is shown when Activity B cannot start until Activity A is complete?
questions.n: A finish-to-start relationship is the classic sequential dependency.

questions.q: Which operative word traditionally indicates that the Contractor is permitted to exercise an option?
questions.n: 'May' expresses permission or an allowed option.

questions.q: A ceremony is scheduled immediately after the final structural beam is placed. What milestone has been reached?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction
questions.n: The final frame member marks topping out.

questions.q: Which operative word is traditionally used for an informational statement describing action by the Owner or another party rather than directing the Contractor?
questions.n: 'Will' is commonly used for information about actions by the Owner or others, rather than contractor commands.

questions.q: What term refers to the initial capital cost required to construct a project?
questions.n: First cost is the initial expenditure associated with constructing or acquiring the facility.

questions.q: In construction specifications, what does 'install' generally mean?
o: Place in position, incorporate into the Work, adjust, clean, and make ready for use
questions.n: Specification definitions of 'install' extend beyond delivery to complete placement and readiness for service.

questions.q: What activity relationship requires one activity to finish before the next begins?
questions.n: Sequential logic places activities one after another.

questions.q: Under legacy ACI 318 provisions commonly cited in older construction references, how long were concrete material/test records required to be retained after project completion?
questions.n: Legacy ACI 318 provisions required complete records of concrete/material tests to be retained for at least two years after completion, subject to longer local requirements.

questions.q: When some work can begin before the preceding activity is fully complete, what general scheduling strategy is being used?
questions.n: Overlapping logic permits a successor to start before full completion of the preceding activity, subject to defined restraints.
